title: Polyglot resumable generator APIs for streamed tools and structured outputs
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Goal: provide idiomatic, resumable generator-style APIs in TypeScript, Python, and Go that unify streaming model tokens, tool/function calls, and structured JSON emission while providing a compatibility shim for older SDKs. This ticket covers interface proposals, minimal reference implementations, and example usage patterns focusing on: 

- backpressure and consumer-driven pacing (async iterators, channels)
- resumable checkpoints (save/restore cursor + KV-cache pointers)
- typed structured outputs with best-effort schema validation and incremental emission
- graceful fallback for old SDKs that only support non-streaming responses

Requirements are intentionally low-level: provide stable primitives that SDKs and customers can compose into higher-level helpers (chat loop managers, tool runners, eval harnesses). The deliverables: interface docs, 3 reference examples (TS/Py/Go), a short compatibility shim, and tests demonstrating resume and fallback flows.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc with concrete API surface for JS/Python/Go (async iterator, generator, channel) reviewed by SDK leads
Reference implementation for each language that compiles/passes linters and includes unit tests for resume + backpressure
Example that wires a streaming tool invocation where the model emits a structured JSON chunk, then a tool is invoked mid-stream and the client resumes afterwards
Compatibility shim that transforms legacy non-stream responses into an async-iterator-like experience (buffering strategy documented)
Performance regression check: added overhead < 4% on p50 latency for a noop stream when enabled
notes: We prefer minimal runtime allocations in Go and explicit backpressure signals in JS to avoid unbounded memory growth.

Resumability design: persist a tuple (request_id, last_token_index, kv_cache_digest) to allow exact resume against the runtime. This is a contract between client SDK and runtime; server work needed separately.

For structured outputs we will adopt a schema-first validation helper that can accept JSON Schema or a light typed descriptor. Validation errors are emitted as a separate event type so downstream consumers can choose to accept or reject partial output.
Discussed with infra: saving small resume cursors to customer storage is acceptable; encrypt by default for Private deployments.
